chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Imran ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Mada'ini, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
When the Imam intends to know something, Allah lets him know that.

key_terms.أَعْلَمَهُ: He informed him or made him know
key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the One who grants this knowledge
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the Imam, the divinely appointed leader

ai.seo_question: How does the Imam know what he intends to know according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when the Imam intends to know a matter, Allah grants him knowledge of it. It indicates a divinely granted mode of knowledge associated with the Imam's station.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Imran Bin Musa, from Musa Bin Ja’far, from Amro Bin Saeed Al Madainy, from Abu Ubeyda Al Madainy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Whenever the Imam<sup>asws</sup> intends to know something, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> let him<sup>asws</sup> know that’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Umrah ibn Musa from Musa ibn Ja‘far from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id al-Mada’ini from abu ‘Ubayda al-Mada’ini from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“When the Imam (a.s.) would will to know something Allah will grant him such knowledge.”
